newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica sees mine safety laws in place by January.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica sees mine safety laws in place by January.

text.p: South Africa's Inspector of Mines Derek Baker said on Tuesday new legislation to prevent a repeat of the 1995 Vaal Reefs gold mine accident, which killed 104 miners, would be in place by January.
The new Mine Health and Safety Act, already approved by cabinet, was geared to ensuring improved training and safety standards on mines, he added.

"It is expected that the Act will come into operation on December 1, or January 1 at the latest. It is hoped that this will prevent a similar accident occurring again in the future," he told a parliamentary committee on mines and energy.
The May 10, 1995 accident, at Vaal Reefs Exploration and Mining Co Ltd, was the worst in the country's history.
It occurred when an underground locomotive plummeted down a mine shaft, crushing a lift-cage and killing the workers inside.

Briefing MPs on the Vaal Reefs tragedy, Baker said an investigation into the underground locomotives at the mines had found 50 percent were "bridged", or short-circuited -- a major breach of safety rules and cited as the cause of the disaster.

Judge Ramon Leon, chairing a joint commission of inquiry and inquest into the accident, recommended the prosecution of several mine employees and held Vaal Reefs liable for culpable homicide. The Attorney-General's office is studying the report and must decide whether to prosecute.
The National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) on Tuesday welcomed the setting of an implementation date, saying the new laws would for the first time allow workers a say in their workplace safety.
"We see the Act as one of NUM's achievements because previously workers had no access to the codes of practise on safety," NUM spokesman Ben Molapo told Reuters.
"Now for the first time workers will be trained in health and safety standards, and will be able to fully participate and have an input in ensuring that we work in safety," he said.
The Chamber of Mines employer grouping could not immediately be reached for comment.
